benchmark_proposal.protocol: One release build with frozen source/tool hashes; fixed 256 successful resolutions plus 256 target consumptions per trial; one warmup and five captured trials, serial one process/job. Record median/p95 elapsed and child peak RSS. Native timing parity requires the same observable fixture in the pinned native runtime.
proposed_ranges: Preserve every output, error disposition and snapshot guard.
For 4096 nodes, target a warm median below 100 ms for the 256-lookup batch on the current host; calibrate any absolute gate from captured environmental evidence.
After indexing, target less than 2.5x query-time growth from 1024 to 4096 nodes. Current linear scans risk approximately 4x growth.
For ordinary 256-element label/selection work, avoid UI-thread long tasks above 50 ms. Work exceeding 100 ms needs progress and cancellation rather than an unexplained stall.

integration_gap.evidence: The current F36 runnable Rust source/manifests contain no dependencies or calls for syson-general-view, syson-imports, syson-references, syson-view-usage, syson-semantic-names or syson-semantic-validation. F44 qualifies unchanged source and F45 is not wired into that UI.
integration_gap.expected: Users should actually create/import, navigate effective names, see source-positioned warnings and reload supported data inside the application before those workflows can be considered at parity.
integration_gap.plan: Use small integration PRs per user task after prerequisites land; do not merge all 33 units or treat API tests as proof of integrated application behavior.
